Covariates dropped for collinearity that matter for prediction

Source: R/attgt_functions.R
unsupported_covariates.Rd

A model fitted on one sample (the units with D == 0) and used to predict for another (D == 1) cannot identify coefficients on covariates that are collinear in the fitting sample, so such covariates are dropped. That is harmless when, for a predicted unit, the dropped column equals the same linear combination of the kept columns as in the fitting sample (duplicate columns, a factor level no unit has). Otherwise, e.g. a dummy for a region that only treated units belong to, the prediction implicitly sets that coefficient to zero and extrapolates for the unit.

This function flags, for each unit with D == 1 and each dropped covariate, whether that unit's prediction is affected. It is the check behind pte_attgt()'s warning about dropped covariates, exported so that other attgt_funs can apply the same rule, combine flags across fitting samples, weight them, and report them with pte_cell_warning(). To fit on treated units and predict for comparison units, pass 1 - D.

Usage

unsupported_covariates(covmat, D, keep_covs = NULL)

Arguments

covmat

numeric covariate matrix for all units, including the intercept; column names are used in the result.

D

indicator (0/1 or logical): 0 for the units the model is fitted on, 1 for the units it predicts for.

keep_covs

indices of the columns of covmat kept in the fitted model. The default NULL uses the rule in pte_attgt(): a pivoted QR decomposition of the fitting sample's crossprod(covmat) / n, keeping the first rank columns.

Value

A logical matrix with one row per unit with D == 1 (in the order of covmat) and one column per dropped covariate that is TRUE for at least one of them. TRUE means that unit's value is not the fitting sample's linear combination of the kept columns. With no such covariates it has zero columns.

Examples

set.seed(1)
D <- rep(0:1, each = 10)
region_c <- c(rep(0, 10), rep(1:0, 5)) # region "c" has treated units only
covmat <- cbind("(Intercept)" = 1, x = rnorm(20), region_c = region_c,
                x_copy = NA)
covmat[, "x_copy"] <- 2 * covmat[, "x"] # redundant for every unit
flags <- unsupported_covariates(covmat, D)
colnames(flags) # "region_c" only
#> [1] "region_c"
colMeans(flags) # share of treated units affected
#> region_c 
#>      0.5
